# clavis secrets duplicates

<p class="cli-lead">Find secrets that share a value, in one environment or across environments</p>

<div class="cli-usage">

```sh
clavis secrets duplicates [flags]
```

</div>

Find secrets that share a value. It reports two kinds: different keys
in one environment holding the same value (one credential copied under
two names), and the same key holding the same value in several
environments, which is flagged when production shares a value with a
non-production environment, because a leak in dev would then expose
production.

Only secrets of kind `secret` with at least 6 characters are compared,
so settings such as `true` or `3000` do not show up. Values are fetched
(the read is audited) and compared on your computer; they are never
printed, and neither is anything derived from them.

## Examples

```sh
clavis secrets duplicates
```

<p class="cli-example-title">Only inside one environment</p>

```sh
clavis secrets duplicates --only-env production
```

```sh
clavis secrets duplicates --json
```
